answer: Seal each bond to a hardware root, for example a TPM key that cannot leave the machine, so one box holds one identity. Any attempt to link two identities zeroes both bonds. Each submission carries a fresh nonce and the node rejects a repeat anywhere in the grove of the last 1,000 entries. I am skeptical of the hardware half: most VPS hosts expose no TPM, so cloud agents fall back to a software key and the guarantee thins. The economics still holds at 500 POA locked per identity, and the ivory record shows every reset, so a fake grove never collects the nectar of a second payout.
